model.name: Each natural class OWNS its name — derives its own display name from its content (derivedName; displayName overrides, originalName preserved)
model.description: The DERIVATION half of the naming design (pairs with R40.104 rename = the OVERRIDE half). Each natural class COMPUTES ITS OWN display name from its content — Image from its capture datetime, Email from its subject, Contact from its full name, CalendarEntry from its title+date, File from a clean basename — the class owns its name, no external namer. THREE names: derivedName (what the CLASS computes), displayName (what the USER sets — WINS when present, R40.104), originalName (the raw input string — PRESERVED but NEVER shown as the name). Display resolves displayName ?? derivedName; originalName is never the displayed name. Scenario-first-retroactive: the expert is already building this (increment #3) — this req routes the in-flight work so it is traceable, not orphaned in code.

discoverySource.note: Expert building the derivation as increment #3 with no req behind it (build-ahead-of-req = the orphan pattern). PO-authorized 2026-09-06 to route the in-flight work so it is traceable.

model.queuePriority: TIER-A — expert increment #3 (rename prep), AHEAD of R40.104 rename (#4).
model.crossRefNote: DERIVATION half of the naming design; R40.104 is the OVERRIDE half (two halves of one design). Extends R40.99 (the natural class owns its behaviour — here, its name-derivation, alongside toUnit/fromUnit/render). R37.15 (store-once, don't-embed-a-derived-field) is the STORED-name discipline, distinct + compatible.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Each natural class DERIVES its own display name from its content: Image from capture datetime, Email from subject, Contact from full name, CalendarEntry from title+date, File from a clean basename. The class owns the derivation — there is no external namer/free naming function for a type.

gateRef.assertion: each natural class computes its own derivedName from its content; an external namer or a class not deriving its own name => RED

acceptanceCriteria.stubMustFail: seed a free naming function (or an external namer) computing a class's name outside the class -> RED

acceptanceCriteria.text: originalName (the raw input string) is PRESERVED on the object but NEVER shown as the object's name (this is the string we were wrongly displaying).

gateRef.assertion: originalName is stored + never rendered as the name; originalName shown as the name => RED

acceptanceCriteria.stubMustFail: seed the raw originalName rendered as the object's name -> RED

acceptanceCriteria.text: derivedName is the FALLBACK display name when no displayName (user override, R40.104) is set: displayed name = displayName ?? derivedName. With no displayName, the class's derivedName shows.

gateRef.assertion: displayed name = displayName if set else derivedName; a no-displayName object showing anything other than its derivedName => RED

acceptanceCriteria.stubMustFail: seed an object with no displayName that shows something other than its derivedName -> RED

acceptanceCriteria.text: Name-derivation is registered PER CLASS: a 7th class derives its own name with ZERO central-switch edits — both open-set and closed-set lints stay 0 (no if/switch enumerating classes for naming).

gateRef.assertion: adding a class's name-derivation requires no central switch edit; a switch/if-chain enumerating classes for naming => RED

acceptanceCriteria.stubMustFail: seed a central switch enumerating classes to decide name-derivation -> RED

acceptanceCriteria.text: The three-name model is CONSISTENT with R40.104 rename: derivedName (class-computed, this req) + displayName (user-set, wins, R40.104) + originalName (preserved, never shown). The two reqs are two halves of ONE naming design — no divergent name model.

gateRef.assertion: the derivedName/displayName/originalName model matches across R40.105 (derive) + R40.104 (override); a divergent name model => RED

acceptanceCriteria.stubMustFail: seed a name model where displayName does not win over derivedName, or the two reqs disagree -> RED
